title: Israeli strike on Gaza aid van kills three as army says victims were Islamic Jihad members
summary: Three men were killed when an Israeli drone struck a van carrying food for displaced people in Gaza City on Saturday; the military said on Sunday they were Islamic Jihad operatives, while witnesses described a vehicle about to distribute food to children. Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,671 people have been killed since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025.
content:
An Israeli drone strike killed three men in a van carrying food for displaced people in Gaza City on Saturday, in an attack that has become the latest flashpoint in the dispute over a ceasefire that, on paper, has been in force for more than a year.

The strike hit the vehicle in the Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood, on Al-Sina'a Street in the west of the city, as it was about to hand out food and drink to families sheltering in tents, according to Gaza's civil defence agency and witnesses cited by [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/21/at-least-four-palestinians-killed-in-israeli-attacks-on-gaza). Al-Shifa Hospital confirmed it had received the bodies of the three men, and several other people were wounded.

"It was just about to stop to distribute the food and drinks to children, and then it was hit by a missile," Abu Zein al-Daya, a displaced Gaza resident who witnessed the attack, told reporters. "The target is anyone who is giving the people food."

Papers found inside the van bore the logo of World Central Kitchen, the aid organisation that distributes food across Gaza. The charity said in a statement that the vehicle was not affiliated with it, and that while its driver had previously worked for the organisation, the two other men in the vehicle were not its employees. The distinction matters: in a territory where food distribution is one of the few lifelines left, the question of who was in the van — and what it was carrying — has become central to how the strike is understood.

On Sunday, the Israeli military gave its own account. It said the three men killed were members of Palestinian Islamic Jihad, including a company commander in the group's engineering unit, and that they had been falsely presented as aid workers. The military identified them as Ahmad Badran Nimer Sawafiri, the commander, along with Mustafa Yousef Mustafa Rifai and Khaled Od Fathi Na'im. It said the vehicle was being used to transport food and logistical supplies to members of the organisation, and that it bore no markings identifying it as belonging to a humanitarian group.

The competing accounts could not be independently verified on the day, and they illustrate a pattern that has repeated throughout the war: an incident involving a civilian-looking vehicle, followed by sharply different claims about who was inside and why it was hit. What is not in dispute is that three people are dead, that the van was carrying packaged food, and that the strike took place in a neighbourhood where displaced families were waiting for it.

The van was not the only killing on Saturday. Gaza's civil defence agency said a Palestinian man was shot dead by Israeli gunfire in the Halawa displacement camp, east of the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, and his body was taken to al-Shifa Hospital. Earlier in the day, an attack on a young man riding an electric bicycle in al-Mawasi, in Khan Younis in southern Gaza, wounded three people, who were taken to Nasser Medical Complex. On Friday, Palestinian media reported that four people had been killed in an Israeli airstrike in the Bureij area of central Gaza.

Taken together, the deaths underline how little the ceasefire has changed daily life in the territory. The truce came into force in October 2025, but Gaza's Health Ministry said on Saturday that 1,671 people have been killed since then, and Al Jazeera's correspondent in Gaza City reported more than 600 ceasefire violations over the same period. The ministry puts the total death toll since Israel launched its war on Gaza three years ago at 74,736.

The strike also comes as winter deepens the humanitarian crisis. Heavy rain and flooding have swamped tens of thousands of tents, and the World Food Programme warned this week that Palestinians have been forced to burn rubbish to cook their food. "Now even the rubbish is wet," Shaun Hughes, the programme's country director for Palestine, said. The International Organization for Migration says more than 100,000 tents sitting in Egypt cannot be delivered to Gaza because of strict Israeli conditions on entry, including limits on the diameter of the tents' central poles. "Usually anything under 38 millimetres is OK; anything above, it's usually deemed as not acceptable," Hughes explained, adding that the aid agencies are given no specifics about why particular shipments are refused.

The violence is not confined to Gaza. Late on Friday, Hamza Masoud Salim Abdo, 42, was shot dead by security guards from an Israeli settlement near the village of Dura al-Qari, north of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry, which said his body was being withheld by Israeli authorities. Another man was detained during the incident. Al Jazeera's correspondent in Ramallah reported that settler attacks are being carried out with "impunity", noting that fewer than 3 percent of Israeli attacks that are investigated lead to a partial or full conviction.

The incident in Gaza City will now test the fragile structures built around the ceasefire. The [Board of Peace](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/board-of-peace-faults-israel-hamas-gaza-ceasefire-november-2026), the US-led body set up to oversee the truce, has already faulted both sides over violations, and each new killing adds pressure on the mediators to show that the agreement can restrain the fighting rather than simply record it. For the families in Tel al-Hawa, the question is more immediate: whether the next van carrying food to their tents will arrive at all. The pattern of strikes on civilian areas is not unique to Gaza — a [Russian drone strike on an apartment block near Kyiv](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/russian-drone-strike-dymer-apartment-block-november-2026) this week left residents missing under the rubble — but in Gaza, where almost the entire population is displaced and dependent on aid, every interruption to food distribution is felt within hours.

Note: the photograph accompanying this article shows damage to buildings in the Gaza Strip and is used for illustration; it does not depict the van struck on 21 November.
